Notes: Joseph Osterman moved to Galveston from Baltimore in 1838; documented individual Jewish presence
Jews were living in Velasco, Bolivar, Nacogdoches, Goliad, San Antonio, and Galveston by 1838; presence of a few individuals
First Jewish cemetery in Texas dedicated in 1852 (Jewish Cemetery Association organized); organized community
First Jewish services held at home of Isadore Dyer
By 1868 an estimated 125 Jews lived on the island; B'nai Israel founded 1868
41 members of the Jewish community perished in the 8 Sept 1900 hurricane (death toll; not population)
Approximately 1000 Jews lived in Galveston by 1907; Galveston Movement 1907-1914 brought ~10000 immigrants who mostly dispersed
